w-ng-004.title: Ogbono Soup (Draw Soup)

instructions.1: If using whole ogbono seeds, grind them using a mortar and pestle or a coffee grinder. Skip this step if using pre-ground seeds.
instructions.2: In a large pot, add some palm oil on low heat and add the ogbono seeds.
instructions.3: Mix in the ogbono seeds and break any lumps with a serving spoon. Stir until it’s thoroughly coated.
instructions.4: Add the stock and stir. Add about a cup at a time until you reach your desired thickness. If you don't have enough stock, add water.
instructions.5: Bring to a boil, then set to low heat and let it cook for about 10 minutes, stirring intermittently.
instructions.6: Add the meats and spices.
instructions.7: Taste for salt and add some if needed.
instructions.8: If it becomes too thick, add a little more water.
instructions.10: Add the chopped spinach and let simmer on low for about 2 more minutes.
instructions.11: Your ogbono soup is ready to serve!

w-ng-004.culturalNotes: Ogbono soup is a popular dish in Nigeria, often served with rice or fufu.

w-ng-005.title: Edikang Ikong (Nigerian Vegetable Soup)

instructions.1: Wash the goat meat thoroughly and cut it into small pieces. Place it in a pot and add 2 cups of water. Bring it to a boil over medium heat for 30 minutes until it is half-cooked.
instructions.2: Add the bouillon powder, black pepper, salt, and onion. Let it boil for 10 minutes.
instructions.3: Wash the waterleaf and ugwu leaves thoroughly and cut them into small pieces.
instructions.4: Add the waterleaf and ugwu leaves to the pot. Let them boil for 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Add the palm oil, smoked fish, shrimp, and ground crayfish. Let the mixture boil for 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Add the cayenne pepper and let the soup boil for 5 minutes.
instructions.7: Turn off the heat and serve the soup hot.

w-ng-005.culturalNotes: Edikang Ikong is a traditional Nigerian vegetable soup known for its rich flavor and green leaves.

w-ng-006.title: Efo Riro - Nigerian Spinach Stew

instructions.1: Wash the spinach thoroughly and chop it.
instructions.2: In a large pot, heat the palm oil over medium heat.
instructions.3: Add the chopped onion, habanero pepper, red bell pepper, and tomatoes, and stir for 5 minutes until the onion becomes translucent.
instructions.4: Add the cooked beef or goat meat and mushrooms, and continue stirring for 3 minutes.
instructions.5: Add the spinach, bouillon powder, ground crayfish, cayenne pepper, black pepper, and salt, and stir well.
instructions.6: Add the water or stock, bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat and let it simmer for 20 minutes.
instructions.7: Add the pepper flakes if desired, and continue cooking for an additional 5 minutes.
instructions.8: Serve the stew hot with rice or fufu.

w-ng-006.culturalNotes: Efo Riro is a popular dish in Nigeria, typically served with rice or fufu.

w-ng-007.title: Ewedu Soup

instructions.1: Wash the jute leaves thoroughly if using fresh, or let them thaw if using frozen.
instructions.2: Place the jute leaves in a pot and add enough water to cover them.
instructions.3: Add the ground crayfish, salt, iru (if using), pepper, and bouillon.
instructions.4: Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat, then reduce the heat and simmer for 20-30 minutes until the leaves are tender.
instructions.5: Serve the soup hot with rice or fufu.

w-ng-007.culturalNotes: Ewedu is a traditional Nigerian soup often served with rice or fufu.

w-ng-008.title: Fried Plantain

instructions.1: Heat a thin layer of vegetable oil in a frying pan.
instructions.2: Meanwhile, cut the plantain into long, oblong slices.
instructions.3: Fry the slices in the oil on both sides until golden brown.
instructions.4: Sprinkle the fried plantain immediately with salt or brown sugar to taste.
instructions.5: Serve hot.

w-ng-008.culturalNotes: Fried plantain is a popular dish in Nigeria, served as a side or part of a main meal.

w-ng-009.title: Kuli-kuli

instructions.1: Toast the peanuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat, stirring occasionally to avoid burning. Once roasted, remove the skins by rubbing them between your hands or using a cloth to gently press and peel off the skins.
instructions.2: Using a food processor or blender, grind the roasted peanuts to form a peanut butter, working in batches as necessary. This will take around 5-10 minutes depending on power.
instructions.3: Transfer the peanut mixture to a large mixing bowl. Add water, ¼ cup (60 ml) at a time, to the peanut butter, kneading with your hands after each addition. This will swell up the grains in the peanut butter, making it thicker and releasing the oils. Stop adding water once the mixture starts releasing oils. Continue to knead for a further 5 minutes to release as much oil as possible.
instructions.4: Put the mixture into a cheesecloth, and squeeze to release the oils. Transfer the peanut mixture back to the bowl, and set aside the oils for deep-frying.
instructions.5: Stir in the remaining ingredients, mixing well to combine.
instructions.6: Mix in enough water, a tablespoon at a time, until you get a moldable dough, and knead well.
instructions.7: Take teaspoonfuls of the dough and roll them into small balls or form them into flat discs, depending on your preference. You can also shape them into small cylinders or oval shapes, like traditional kuli-kuli. You can experiment with different shapes.
instructions.8: Heat the reserved oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry the kuli-kuli pieces in batches, ensuring they don’t overcrowd the pan, until they are golden brown and crispy on all sides (about 4-5 minutes). Be sure to flip them carefully to ensure even frying.
instructions.9: Once fried, remove the kuli-kuli from the oil and place them on a paper towel to drain excess oil. Allow them to cool completely before serving.

w-ng-009.culturalNotes: Kuli-kuli is a traditional Nigerian snack or breakfast dish.

w-ng-010.title: Ofada Rice

instructions.1: Wash the rice thoroughly with water until the rinse water is clear.
instructions.2: Add the rice to a large pot and add enough water to cover the rice by about 2 cm.
instructions.3: Add salt to taste.
instructions.4: Cover the pot and bring the rice to a boil over high heat.
instructions.5: Reduce the heat and let the rice simmer for 20 minutes or until cooked.
instructions.6: Turn off the heat and let the rice rest for 5 minutes before serving.

w-ng-010.culturalNotes: Ofada rice is a local variety of rice in Nigeria, known for its unique flavor and dark brown color.

w-ng-011.title: Ofe Owerri

w-ng-011-i9.name: fresh bell pepper or chile pepper

instructions.1: Clean the meats and dryfish, and cut into pieces.
instructions.2: Add the meats to a pot with seasoning cubes and water and bring to a boil until tender.
instructions.3: Add the dryfish and smoked fish and simmer for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Stir in the cocoyam paste to thicken the soup, making sure it's well incorporated.
instructions.5: Stir in the palm oil, crayfish, ogiri, and pepper and simmer for 5-10 minutes.
instructions.6: Add okazi leaves and simmer for 3 minutes.
instructions.7: Stir in ugu leaves and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
instructions.8: Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve hot with pounded yam or fufu.

w-ng-011.culturalNotes: Ofe Owerri is a traditional soup from Imo State in Nigeria, typically served with pounded yam or fufu.

w-ng-012.title: Owo Soup

w-ng-012-i3.name: Goat meat or assorted halal meat

instructions.1: Blend the tomatoes and fresh pepper to a paste.
instructions.2: Combine the meat, onion, seasoning cubes, and salt in a pot. Cook for about 3 minutes in its own juices.
instructions.3: Cover the meat with water and simmer until tender.
instructions.4: Add the dried fish, tomato-pepper paste, and ground crayfish to the meat. Add about a cup of water and stir. Let simmer for 10 minutes, stirring to prevent burning.
instructions.5: Dissolve the potash powder in 4 tablespoons of hot water. Strain the mixture carefully and mix the liquid into the soup.
instructions.6: Turn off the heat and allow the soup to cool for about 10 minutes.
instructions.7: Return the soup to the heat and gradually stir in the palm oil.
instructions.8: Remove from the heat and serve with plantains, yam, or any swallow of choice.

w-ng-012.culturalNotes: Owo Soup is a traditional Nigerian dish, typically served with plantains, yam, or any swallow of choice.

w-ng-013.title: Peanut Stew with Beef & Spinach

instructions.1: Cube the beef and brown it in vegetable oil.
instructions.2: Add the onions and garlic and cook for several minutes until the onions start to soften and even color a bit.
instructions.3: Pour in the beef broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the liquid reduces by half.
instructions.4: Stir in the unsweetened peanut butter until well incorporated.
instructions.5: Add the tomatoes and spinach and cook until the spinach wilts and the peanut butter releases its oils, making the dish shiny.

w-ng-013.culturalNotes: Peanut stew is a popular dish in Nigeria, often served with flatbread like kisra or rice.

w-ng-014.title: Nigerian Ogbono Soup with Pounded Yam

w-ng-014-i1.name: Meat (oxtail, stew beef, tripe, cow skin)

instructions.1: Wash the meat and soak it in water for 30 minutes, then drain it.
instructions.2: Place the meat in a pot and cover it with water. Add the onion and bouillon and bring to a boil over low heat for an hour.
instructions.3: Add the smoked fish, ground crayfish, greens, palm oil, and red pepper flakes. Cook for an additional 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the ground egusi and ground ogbono and stir well. Cook for 10 minutes until thickened.
instructions.5: Add salt and pepper to taste. Cook for an additional 5 minutes.
instructions.6: In another pot, place the pounded yam and bring to a boil over low heat for 10 minutes until soft.
instructions.7: Serve the soup with the pounded yam hot.

w-ng-014.culturalNotes: Nigerian Ogbono Soup with Pounded Yam is a traditional dish in Nigeria, known for its rich flavor and creamy texture.

w-gr-001.title: Diples

instructions.1: Mix the flour with water to make a firm dough.
instructions.2: Let the dough rest for 30 minutes.
instructions.3: Cut the dough into small pieces and roll them out thinly.
instructions.4: Fry the pieces in hot oil until golden brown.
instructions.5: Drain the diples on paper towels.
instructions.6: Pour the melted butter and honey over the diples, and add cinnamon.
instructions.7: Serve hot or cold as desired.

w-gr-001.culturalNotes: Diples are a traditional Greek sweet served on special occasions.

w-gr-002.title: Galaktoboureko

instructions.1: Combine sugar, eggs, and semolina in a saucepan. Add milk and vanilla beans. Stir in lemon juice.
instructions.2: Bring the mixture to a boil, stirring constantly with a fork. When it starts boiling, reduce heat and keep stirring for another 10 minutes. Remove the mixture from the heat and let it cool.
instructions.3: Brush each sheet of phyllo dough with melted butter.
instructions.4: Butter a pan and place half the phyllo sheets in it, one by one. Pour the cooled semolina custard over the pastry, and cover with the remaining buttered phyllo.
instructions.5: Sprinkle the pastry with a bit of water.
instructions.6: Bake the pastry in a preheated oven at 180°C for 1 hour. Let it cool before serving.

w-gr-002.culturalNotes: Galaktoboureko is a traditional Greek dessert made from a custard of milk and semolina, wrapped in phyllo dough. It is typically served cold.

w-gr-003.title: Giouvetsi (Traditional Greek Orzo Bake)

instructions.1: Heat olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat; cook meat until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
instructions.2: Add pureed tomatoes, garlic, sugar, salt, and pepper. Cover and simmer for 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Set aside.
instructions.3: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
instructions.4: Melt butter in a medium skillet over medium heat and add the orzo. Saute until slightly brown, 3 to 5 minutes.
instructions.5: Transfer orzo to a baking pan, spreading it out evenly. Place the meat on top of the orzo and pour the tomato sauce over the meat. Add hot water.
instructions.6: Cover with aluminum foil and bake in the preheated oven until all water is absorbed and orzo is soft, about 1 hour. If the dish becomes too dry, add more water during baking.

w-gr-003.culturalNotes: Giouvetsi is a traditional Greek dish often served on special occasions. It is usually served with Greek salad.

w-gr-004.title: Air Fryer Beef Kofta Kebabs

instructions.1: Mix the ground beef, onion, parsley, garlic, cumin, coriander, salt, black pepper, and cinnamon in a large bowl until well combined.
instructions.2: Divide the mixture into 8 portions and shape them into oval-shaped patties around the skewers, making sure the point of the skewer is covered.
instructions.3: Place the kebabs on a plate and refrigerate.
instructions.4: Preheat the air fryer to 370 degrees F (188 degrees C).
instructions.5: Stir the yogurt, cucumber, garlic, lemon juice, dill, and kosher salt together in a small bowl and refrigerate until ready to use.
instructions.6: Place 4 skewers in the basket of the air fryer and cook for 10 minutes. Transfer the kebabs to a plate. Repeat with the remaining skewers.
instructions.7: Serve the kebabs with tzatziki sauce.

w-gr-004.culturalNotes: Kofta is a popular dish in many Arab and Middle Eastern countries, often served with tzatziki sauce.

w-gr-005.title: Melomakarono

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
instructions.2: Whisk flour, cinnamon, baking powder, cloves, baking soda, and nutmeg together in a large bowl.
instructions.3: In a separate bowl, beat butter until light and fluffy; add sugar and mix well.
instructions.4: Beat egg yolks and orange juice together in another bowl. Stir egg mixture into the butter mixture gradually while mixing.
instructions.5: Add flour mixture slowly to the butter mixture, mixing after each addition. Add honey and mix until a soft dough forms.
instructions.6: Cover the dough and chill it until firm enough to work with, about 30 minutes.
instructions.7: Shape the dough into small ovals and place them a few inches apart on baking sheets. Flatten slightly; cookies will spread.
instructions.8: Bake in the preheated oven until light golden brown, 15 to 20 minutes.
instructions.9: Meanwhile, heat honey, water, and sugar together in a saucepan over medium-low heat until sugar is dissolved. Let syrup cool.
instructions.10: Mix walnuts, cinnamon, and cloves together in a bowl to make the topping.
instructions.11: Dip cookies into the cooled syrup for 10 to 15 seconds per side. Sprinkle walnut topping over syrup and let dry completely.
instructions.12: Store cookies in muffin cups or between layers of parchment paper.

w-gr-005.culturalNotes: Melomakarono is a traditional Greek cookie usually served during Christmas.

w-gr-006.title: Nettle Soup

instructions.1: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with 2 teaspoons of salt. Add the stinging nettles and cook for 1-2 minutes until they soften. This will remove most of the sting. Drain in a colander and rinse with cold water. Trim off any tough stems and chop coarsely.
instructions.2: Heat the olive oil in a saucepan over medium-low heat, and stir in the onion. Cook until the onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in the rice, chicken broth, and chopped nettles. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender, about 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Puree the soup with an immersion blender, and season to taste with salt and pepper.

w-gr-006.culturalNotes: Stinging nettles are a plant that grows naturally in Greece and are used in many traditional recipes.

w-gr-007.title: Greek Orange Phyllo Cake (Portokalopita)

instructions.1: Combine 2 cups sugar, 1.5 cups water, and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Squeeze in orange juice and add juiced halves. Bring to a boil and boil vigorously for 8 minutes. Remove from heat and allow the syrup to cool.
instructions.2: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking pan.
instructions.3: Remove phyllo sheets from the package and tear or slice them into shreds. Place the shredded phyllo in the baking pan and let it dry out a little.
instructions.4: Cut 1 orange in half and slice 1 half into very thin half-moons to garnish the cake. Zest and juice the remaining 2 1/2 oranges.
instructions.5: Combine orange juice, orange zest, eggs, Greek yogurt, olive oil, 0.5 cup sugar, and baking powder in a blender or food processor. Blend until the mixture is smooth and all ingredients are well combined.
instructions.6: Pour the mixture over the shredded phyllo in the baking pan. Stir gently to ensure the wet mixture is evenly distributed and no dry phyllo shreds remain. Garnish the top of the cake with the orange slices.
instructions.7: Bake in the preheated oven until the top is golden and the filling is set, about 45 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the center should come out clean.
instructions.8: Remove the cake from the oven and immediately ladle the cooled syrup over the hot cake.
instructions.9: Set the cake aside for at least 1 hour or overnight, until most of the syrup has soaked in. Slice into squares and serve.

w-gr-007.culturalNotes: Portokalopita is a traditional Greek cake made with phyllo dough and orange, typically served on special occasions.

w-gr-008.title: Pan-Fried White Brined Cheese (Saganaki)

w-gr-008-i1.name: large slice of salty, brined white cheese (e.g. feta, sirene)

instructions.1: Heat a small frying pan over medium-high heat.
instructions.2: While the pan heats, cut the cheese into slices of the desired size and thickness. Thicker slices will take longer to melt through and may result in burning, while thinner ones will have less chance to brown.
instructions.3: Optionally, dredge the slices in flour—this will create a darker and slightly crispier crust, but is an optional step as the cheese will acquire a very slight crust on its own by virtue of the oil and high heat. It will also reduce the spitting somewhat.
instructions.4: Add the oil to the hot pan and swirl it around. When the oil shimmers and seems to become more fluid, it is ready. Add the cheese and step back—it will spit due to the brine-water on the cheese.
instructions.5: Flip the cheese after a minute or two. A slice of ¾ centimeter should get about 1–2 minutes per side.
instructions.6: Serve immediately, with lemon and (optionally) bread.

w-gr-008.culturalNotes: Saganaki is a traditional Greek dish served as an appetizer. It is usually served with lemon and bread.

w-gr-009.title: Spanakorizo

instructions.1: Bring water and rice to a boil in a saucepan. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until rice is tender and liquid has been absorbed, 20 to 25 minutes.
instructions.2: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Saute onion until tender, about 5 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the cooked rice and spinach; cook and stir until spinach wilts, 3 to 5 minutes.
instructions.4: Add lemon juice, zest, feta cheese, and dill. Remove from heat. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

w-gr-009.culturalNotes: Spanakorizo is a traditional Greek dish served as a main or side dish. It is characterized by its fresh and tangy flavors.

w-gr-010.title: Strapatsada with a Chickpea Rice Salad

instructions.1: Shred the tomatoes using a box grater (this should yield about 1 cup grated tomato).
instructions.2: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the grated tomato and garlic. Cook, stirring frequently, until the tomatoes are broken down and most of the water has evaporated, about 7 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the eggs, 1/2 teaspoon of salt, and 1/4 teaspoon of pepper to the tomato mixture. Cook until the eggs are set, gently stirring, about 3 minutes. They should be soft but not watery. Fold in the feta and oregano. Keep warm.
instructions.4: In a large bowl, stir together the rice, chickpeas, olives, parsley, lemon zest, and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon each of salt and pepper. In a small bowl, whisk together the lemon juice and tahini and pour over the rice mixture. Toss gently to coat.
instructions.5: Serve the egg mixture over the rice mixture. If you like, sprinkle with additional tomato, oregano, and parsley.

w-gr-010.culturalNotes: Strapatsada is a traditional Greek dish usually served as an appetizer or a simple main course. This dish combines eggs, tomatoes, and feta cheese, and is easy and quick to prepare.

w-gr-011.title: Taramasalata

instructions.1: Place the bread in a bowl, cover with cold water, and let it sit until well soaked, 5 to 10 minutes. Drain the water from the bowl and squeeze the bread to remove excess water.
instructions.2: Add the bread, olive oil, onion, and lemon juice to a food processor and blend until smooth.
instructions.3: Add the tarama and blend until well combined.

w-gr-011.culturalNotes: Taramasalata is a traditional Greek appetizer, typically served with fresh bread or crackers.

w-gr-012.title: Roasted Garlic Tirokafteri

instructions.1: Place the roasted red peppers, roasted garlic, hot pepper sauce, lemon juice, oregano, and white pepper into a blender and blend until smooth.
instructions.2: Add the crumbled feta and cream cheese, and blend until smooth.
instructions.3: With the blender running, slowly pour in the olive oil until incorporated and thickened.
instructions.4: Stir in the half-and-half if needed to achieve a dip consistency.
instructions.5: Cover and store the dip in the refrigerator until ready to serve.

w-gr-012.culturalNotes: Tirokafteri is a traditional Greek dip served as an appetizer. It is known for its creamy and spicy flavor.

w-gr-013.title: Tomato and Feta Fritters

instructions.1: Gather all ingredients.
instructions.2: Stir together tomatoes, zucchini, green onions, kosher salt, sugar, black pepper, oregano, and cayenne in a bowl. Let sit for 15 minutes for the sugar and salt to draw out liquids from the vegetables.
instructions.3: Stir the tomato mixture; add parsley, mint, and basil. Crumble in feta cheese. Add flour and baking powder; mix with a spoon until combined. The batter should be relatively loose but will hold its shape on a spoon. If too loose, add more flour; if too dry, add some water until desired consistency is reached. Wrap the bowl in plastic wrap and let chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Heat 1 inch of vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), or use a deep fryer.
instructions.5: Place heaping tablespoonfuls of batter in the hot oil; reduce heat to medium. Fry until golden brown and cooked through, 2 to 3 minutes per side.
instructions.6: Flip once more and fry for an additional 30 seconds, if desired.
instructions.7: Serve warm or at room temperature.

w-gr-013.culturalNotes: These fritters are a popular dish in Greece, served as an appetizer or part of a light meal.

w-gr-014.title: Greek Tsoureki

instructions.1: Pour yeast into a small bowl; add warm water and 1/4 cup of flour. Stir, cover with two damp kitchen towels, and leave in a warm place until bubbly, about 2.5 hours.
instructions.2: Combine butter, shortening, and mastic in a saucepan over medium-low heat.
instructions.3: Stir milk and sugar together in another saucepan over medium-low heat until sugar is dissolved and mixture is warm. Remove from heat.
instructions.4: Pour 2 cups flour into the butter mixture and stir well. Add salt, then stir in the yeast mixture. Add 2 more cups of flour and stir well. Stir in 3 beaten eggs. Slowly add the milk mixture and 1 cup of flour and stir well. Add the room-temperature water and the last cup of flour and stir until the dough is not sticky.
instructions.5: Knead dough on a lightly floured surface for 20 minutes with lightly floured hands. Form dough into a ball. Cover with damp towels and let rise in a warm place until doubled in volume, about 2 hours.
instructions.6: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Grease two baking sheets.
instructions.7: Divide dough into two pieces and separate each piece into three strands. Braid each of the 3 strands together to form 2 braided loaves. Place on the baking sheets. Nestle the red-dyed eggs between the strands. Brush the dough with the remaining beaten egg. Sprinkle the tops with almonds and sesame seeds.
instructions.8: Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 25 minutes.

w-gr-014.culturalNotes: Tsoureki is a traditional bread made in Greece during Easter. It is known for its sweet taste and soft texture, and is usually decorated with red-dyed eggs.

w-gr-015.title: Tzatziki Sauce

instructions.1: Line a colander with two layers of cheesecloth; place over a medium bowl. Place the yogurt in the cheesecloth-lined colander, then cover with plastic wrap. Drain the yogurt in the refrigerator for 8 hours to overnight.
instructions.2: Place the grated cucumber on a paper-towel-lined plate; drain for 1 to 2 hours.
instructions.3: Combine the yogurt, cucumber, parsley, mint, lemon juice, garlic, salt, and black pepper in a bowl. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.

w-gr-015.culturalNotes: Tzatziki is a traditional Greek sauce served as an appetizer or with main dishes.

w-gr-016.title: Vasilopita - Greek New Year's Cake

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 175 degrees C (350 degrees F). Generously grease a 10-inch round cake pan.
instructions.2: Beat sugar and butter together in a medium bowl until lighter in color. Add flour and mix until the mixture is mealy. Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
instructions.3: Combine baking powder and milk; add to the egg mixture and mix well. Combine lemon juice and baking soda; stir into the batter. Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan.
instructions.4: Bake the cake in the preheated oven for 20 minutes. Remove and sprinkle the nuts and sugar over the cake, then return it to the oven until the cake springs back to the touch, about 20-30 additional minutes.
instructions.5: Gently cut a small hole in the cake and place a coin in the hole. Try to cover the hole with sugar. Cool the cake on a rack for 10 minutes before inverting it onto a plate.
instructions.6: Serve the cake warm.

w-gr-016.culturalNotes: Vasilopita is a traditional cake served in Greece during New Year's Day.

w-pe-001.title: Peruvian Chicken Soup (Aguadito de Pollo)

w-pe-001-i12.name: potatoes
w-pe-001-i12.standardAmount: 4 Yukon Gold potatoes - cut in half

instructions.1: Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy pot over medium-high heat. Add the onion, garlic, and serrano chili, and cook until the onion has softened, about 1 minute.
instructions.3: Add the chicken and continue to cook for 5 minutes.
instructions.4: Stir in the cilantro, peas, corn, and red pepper; cook for 1 minute.
instructions.5: Pour in the chicken broth, potatoes, and rice. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer until the chicken is opaque and the potatoes are tender, about 40 minutes.

w-pe-001.culturalNotes: Aguadito de Pollo is a traditional Peruvian soup served as a light meal or main dish. It is characterized by a variety of vegetable and spice flavors.

w-pe-002.title: Ají de Gallina

instructions.1: Place chicken breasts, onion, carrot, and 2 cloves of garlic in a large saucepan, pour in 2 quarts of water and slowly bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Skim off the foam which forms on top, then cover, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer until the chicken is tender, about 30 minutes. Remove chicken to a plate and allow to cool. Strain the resulting chicken stock, discarding the vegetables.
instructions.2: Pour evaporated milk and 1/2 cup chicken stock into the bowl of a blender. Add bread cubes and puree until smooth. Add Parmesan cheese and walnuts; puree until smooth. Shred the cooled chicken and discard the bones.
instructions.3: Heat vegetable oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in minced garlic and chopped onion; cook until the onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in shredded chicken and aji amarillo until heated through. Pour in bread puree and cook until hot, stirring frequently. Add more chicken stock if needed to keep from getting too thick.
instructions.4: Stir in turmeric and simmer for 5 minutes more. Serve garnished with hard-cooked egg slices and sprinkled with kalamata olives.

w-pe-002.culturalNotes: Ají de Gallina is a traditional Peruvian dish often served on special occasions.

w-pe-003.title: Ajiaco (Peruvian Beef and Pepper Stew)

w-pe-003-i4.name: Red bell peppers, cut into 1-inch pieces

w-pe-003-i8.name: Baby red potatoes, cut in half

instructions.1: Heat the canola oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the sliced shallots, minced garlic, and red bell peppers. Cook until the shallots have softened and turned translucent, about 4 minutes.
instructions.2: Add the chipotle chile powder and cumin. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
instructions.3: Add the cooked roast beef and red potatoes. Pour in the water and beef broth. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Stir in the oregano, and season to taste with salt and pepper.
instructions.5: Stir in the chopped parsley before serving. Garnish each bowl with a few slices of hard-cooked egg.

w-pe-003.culturalNotes: Ajiaco is a traditional Peruvian dish known for its rich flavors and spicy kick.

w-pe-004.title: Anticucho

instructions.1: Place all the ingredients, except the beef heart, in a bowl and mix thoroughly.
instructions.2: Clean the beef heart, removing all fat. Cut it into bite-sized cubes. Place the heart pieces into the marinade mixture, and leave to marinate for about 10 hours or overnight. The heart should be completely covered by the marinade.
instructions.3: After marinating, thread the meat onto skewers. If desired, at this stage some additional ingredients such as bell peppers or corn-on-cob (cut to a similar size to the heart) may be also added to the skewers.
instructions.4: Cook the skewers on a barbecue grill, turning frequently while brushing with the marinade mix. When the meat is well done, remove skewers from grill and serve immediately.

w-pe-004.culturalNotes: Anticucho is a traditional dish in Peru, often served as a snack or at celebrations.

w-pe-005.title: Arroz Tapado

instructions.1: Bring the rice and 4 cups of water to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender, and the liquid has been absorbed, 20 to 25 minutes.
instructions.2: Place the egg into a saucepan, and cover with water by 1 inch. Cover the saucepan and bring the water to a boil over high heat. Once the water is boiling, remove from the heat and let the egg stand in the hot water for 15 minutes. Pour out the hot water, then cool the egg under cold running water in the sink. Peel once cold. Chop the egg and set aside in a small bowl.
instructions.3: Heat 1 cup of vegetable oil in a deep-fryer or large saucepan to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Deep fry the potato cubes until golden brown, about 5 minutes; drain on paper towels, and set aside.
instructions.4: Place tomatoes and 0.5 cup of water in a blender, and puree until tomatoes are liquefied (peel and seed first, if desired).
instructions.5: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat, and cook and stir the onion, garlic, aji chile powder, cumin, black pepper, and oregano until the onion begins to brown, 8 to 10 minutes; pour in the pureed tomatoes, and simmer for 5 more minutes, stirring often. Mix in the ground beef and carrots, and cook until the meat is no longer pink and the carrots are tender, about 10 minutes. Break the meat up into small chunks as it cooks. Mix in the chopped hard-cooked egg, peas, and peanut butter until thoroughly combined. Finally, gently stir in the cubes of fried potato.
instructions.6: To assemble the dish, oil a flexible plastic bowl (at least 1 cup size) and press cooked rice into the bottom to fill 1/3 of the bowl. Layer about 3/4 inch of meat mixture over the rice, and top with more cooked rice to fill the bowl. With an oiled hand, gently press on the rice to compact the mixture; place a serving plate on top of the bowl, flip, and turn out the rice and meat-filled form. Repeat with remaining ingredients. Garnish with sprinkles of cilantro, chopped tomato, and dollops of ketchup on each serving.

w-pe-005.culturalNotes: Arroz Tapado is a traditional Peruvian dish, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-pe-006.title: Papa a la Huancaína (Huancayo-Style Potatoes)

instructions.1: Place the potatoes in a large pot and cover with salted water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain and set aside to cool slightly.
instructions.2: In a skillet over medium heat, heat the olive oil and cook the onion until tender, about 10 minutes. Remove from heat.
instructions.3: In a small saucepan, bring water to a boil and add the chile peppers. Boil until soft, about 5 minutes. Run the chiles under cold water until cool enough to handle, then remove and discard the skins.
instructions.4: Add the onion, chile peppers, cream cheese, queso fresco, vegetable oil, salt, garlic, and black pepper to a blender and blend until smooth. Stream in the evaporated milk with the blender on until the sauce is creamy.
instructions.5: Arrange 1 lettuce leaf on each of 8 plates. Halve the potatoes and arrange 3 halves on each lettuce leaf. Pour the sauce over the potatoes. Top each serving with a half egg and 2 halves of black olives.

w-pe-006.culturalNotes: Papa a la Huancaína is a traditional Peruvian dish served as an appetizer or light meal.

w-ph-001.title: Purple Yam and Coconut Mochi (Ube Bibingka)

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Line a 9x9-inch baking pan with banana leaves or parchment paper and coat with cooking spray.
instructions.2: Whisk sweet rice flour, rice flour, baking powder, and salt together in a large bowl, then stir in the water and coconut milk. Add ube spread and ube powder. Fold in macapuno and 1 tablespoon muscovado sugar. Pour into the prepared pan.
instructions.3: Bake in the preheated oven until the top starts to crack and the leaves turn brown, about 35 minutes. Brush the top with 1 tablespoon of butter, then bake until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 20 minutes more.
instructions.4: Melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir in 1/4 cup of muscovado sugar; cook, stirring, until it starts to boil. Remove from heat and pour over the warm mochi, covering evenly. Sprinkle with toasted coconut. Let cool for at least 30 minutes.
instructions.5: Use the banana leaves to lift the mochi out of the pan. Cut into 25 small squares; cut the squares diagonally into triangles.

w-ph-001.culturalNotes: Bibingka is a traditional Filipino dessert, often served during holidays and special occasions.

w-ph-002.title: Sago at Gulaman

w-ph-002-i2.name: tapioca pearls
w-ph-002-i2.standardAmount: 1 cup (cooked in boiling water for up to 30 minutes, drained and rinsed until cool)

w-ph-002-i3.name: brown sugar
w-ph-002-i3.standardAmount: 1 cup (boiled with 1 cup water until dissolved, then cooled)

instructions.1: Prepare the agar-agar jelly according to the package instructions (gulaman powder dissolved in water), then cool and dice it.
instructions.2: Boil 1 cup of brown sugar with 1 cup of water until the sugar dissolves, then cool the syrup.
instructions.3: Cook the tapioca pearls in boiling water for up to 30 minutes, then drain and rinse them with cold water until they cool.
instructions.4: In tall glasses, layer the agar-agar jelly, then the tapioca pearls, and finally the cooled brown sugar syrup.
instructions.5: Add crushed ice to the glasses.
instructions.6: Serve the drink with a wide straw (like a milkshake straw) and enjoy the ride.

w-ph-002.culturalNotes: Sago at Gulaman is a traditional Filipino drink, often served during hot weather.

w-pe-007.title: Manjar Blanco

instructions.1: Butter an 8-inch baking dish and set aside.
instructions.2: Mix 0.5 cup water and cornstarch in a bowl until smooth; set aside.
instructions.3: Combine coconut milk, 0.75 cup water, and sugar in a saucepan over low heat and stir until the sugar is dissolved.
instructions.4: Bring the mixture to a boil, add the corn kernels, and stir in the cornstarch mixture, stirring quickly to avoid lumps as it thickens.
instructions.5: Return the mixture to a boil and simmer for 2 minutes, stirring constantly until thick and smooth.
instructions.6: Pour the manjar blanco into the prepared dish and set aside to cool until firm, about 2 hours.
instructions.7: Place the sweetened flaked coconut in a dry skillet over medium heat and stir to toast. Watch carefully so they don't burn. Remove the toasted coconut flakes to a bowl, let cool, and sprinkle over the pudding before serving.

w-pe-007.culturalNotes: Manjar blanco is a traditional Peruvian dessert, often served on special occasions.

w-pe-008.title: Papas Rellenas (Fried Stuffed Potatoes)

instructions.1: Place potatoes into a large pot; cover with salted water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain and allow to steam dry for 1 to 2 minutes. Mash potatoes with 1/2 teaspoon salt in a bowl until no lumps remain. Set aside to cool to room temperature.
instructions.2: Meanwhile, heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir green pepper, onion, and garlic in the hot skillet until onion has softened and turned translucent, about 10 minutes.
instructions.3: Increase heat to medium-high; stir in ground beef. Cook and stir until beef is crumbly and no longer pink. Stir in tomato paste, vinegar, cumin, 1 teaspoon salt, and pepper until tomato paste has dissolved. Transfer beef mixture to a bowl; allow to cool to room temperature.
instructions.4: Line a baking sheet with plastic wrap or waxed paper; set aside. Beat eggs in a mixing bowl; set aside. Pour bread crumbs and flour into separate, shallow dishes; set aside.
instructions.5: Grab a handful of mashed potatoes (about 1/12 of the mashed potatoes); split into 2 equal portions. Form each piece into a small bowl shape and fill each with beef mixture. Place halves together, seal edges, and smooth to make a round ball. Repeat this step with remaining potatoes and beef mixture.
instructions.6: Working one at a time, gently roll potato balls in flour to coat; shake off excess. Dip into beaten egg, then roll in bread crumbs. Gently toss between your hands so any bread crumbs that haven’t stuck can fall away. Place breaded potato balls onto the prepared baking sheet. Refrigerate for 2 to 4 hours or freeze for later use.
instructions.7: Heat oil in a deep fryer or large saucepan to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
instructions.8: Cook potato balls in hot oil in batches, using tongs to roll balls around as they cook to ensure even browning, until crispy and golden brown, about 3 minutes per batch. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate.

w-pe-008.culturalNotes: Papas Rellenas is a traditional Peruvian dish served as a main course or as an appetizer.

w-pe-009.title: Pastel de Choclo

instructions.1: Place eggs in a saucepan and cover with water. Bring to a boil, then remove from heat and let eggs stand in hot water for 15 minutes.
instructions.2: In a skillet over medium heat, add oil, onions, garlic, a pinch of salt, ¼ teaspoon paprika, and black pepper. Cook until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
instructions.3: Add ground beef, remaining 1 teaspoon salt, remaining ¼ teaspoon paprika, and black pepper. Cook and stir until beef is mostly browned, about 5 minutes.
instructions.4: Add chicken, raisins, and olives. Mix well.
instructions.5: Remove eggs from hot water, cool under cold running water, then peel and roughly chop. Add to the beef mixture. Keep the pino warm.
instructions.6: Combine corn and basil in a blender or food processor until smooth. Pour into a saucepan over medium heat. Add butter and cook, stirring until thickened, 7 to 10 minutes.
instructions.7: Add milk, sugar, and salt. Cook until thickened to a paste, about 15 minutes more.
instructions.8: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
instructions.9: Spread the pino into a baking dish. Cover with the corn paste and sprinkle a little sugar on top.
instructions.10: Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown on top, about 20 minutes.

w-pe-009.culturalNotes: Pastel de Choclo is a traditional Peruvian dish, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.
